title: NY State Senate · District 15
area: Central and southern Queens, including Ozone Park, Woodhaven, Howard Beach, Richmond Hill and the Rockaways.

context.text: Incumbent Joseph Addabbo defeated Albert Baldeo in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 77.8% to 21.6% (7,427 to 2,064 votes). He faces Danniel Maio, the Conservative Party nominee, in the general election.

candidates.name: Joseph Addabbo
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary against Albert Baldeo, 77.8% to 21.6%

priorities.text: Describes his role as legislative advocacy for "children, the elderly, families, working people, consumers and veterans," alongside environmental protection, economic development and government accountability.
priorities.quote: children, the elderly, families, working people, consumers and veterans

positions.summary: Has repeatedly opposed the Manhattan Central Business District Tolling Program, introducing legislation to delay its enforcement and arguing it burdens taxi and truck drivers, seniors, people with disabilities, and outer-borough businesses.
positions.quote: While the contradictory program aims to reduce traffic congestion and simultaneously bolster funding for our public transit system from vehicles paying the toll, it also poses significant financial challenges to various groups, including local businesses, taxi drivers, truck operators, the elderly, and individuals with disabilities.

positions.summary: In a January 2013 statement, said he supported the NY SAFE Act gun bill, which he said took steps toward banning assault weapons and curtailing illegal gun sales, though he did not agree with every part of it.
positions.quote: By passing this bill, our state has taken huge steps in addressing the need to ban assault weapons, in considering the mental capability of those owning guns, in curtailing illegal gun sales, and in improving safety in our schools.

record.text: Chairs the Senate Committee on Racing, Gaming and Wagering and the Committee on State-Native American Relations; also serves on the Budget and Revenue, Cities 1, Education, Insurance, Rules, and Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs committees.
Sponsored S10104, which would expand the list of bail-eligible offenses to include offenses involving physical harm or danger to others; remained in the Senate Codes Committee as of April 29, 2026.

Sponsored S10059-A ("Brendon's Law"), which would create new penalties for motor vehicle speed contests, sideshows and street takeovers and authorize vehicle seizure; amended and recommitted to the Senate Transportation Committee on April 28, 2026.

Sponsored S10069, which would enhance know-your-customer and responsible-gaming requirements for mobile sports wagering; remained in the Senate Racing, Gaming and Wagering Committee as of April 27, 2026.

priorities.text: In a 2022 Ballotpedia candidate survey for this same seat, listed crime, schools, and taxes and inflation as his three key campaign messages.
Says he is focused on the needs of seniors and children.

Describes his approach to office as auditing how government spends money: reviewing how officials vote and spend, whether programs actually reach and satisfy the people they are meant to help, and publicizing out-of-order city services and equipment.

positions.summary: Listed stopping congestion pricing in Manhattan among the policy positions he is passionate about.

researchNotes: Danniel Maio has not completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey for this race; his quoted priorities and the congestion-pricing position come from his 2022 survey answers for this same seat (his most recent answers specific to NY Senate District 15), since no more recent statements from him were found.
